historical_references.reference: Al-Bazr ibn Abd al-Muttalib, was a paternal uncle of the Prophet Muhammad and the father of his aunt Umm Hani bint Abu Talib. He is also known as Abu Ja'far Al-Bazr.
historical_references.time_period: Pre-Islamic period to early Islamic period (around 565-632 AD)
historical_references.context: Al-Bazr was an influential figure in Mecca during the pre-Islamic period. He was a member of the Banu Hashim clan and was a very wealthy and influential man. He played a pivotal role in the early Islamic period as well, as he provided shelter to the Prophet Muhammad and his followers during the early years of Islam when they were being persecuted in Mecca.

historical_references.reference: Al-Bazr al-Ansari, was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad and an early convert to Islam. He was also known as Abu Hurairah.
historical_references.context: Al-Bazr al-Ansari was a prominent figure among the early converts to Islam. He was a member of the Ansar tribe in Medina and was known for his extensive knowledge of Hadith (sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad). He was a close companion of the Prophet Muhammad and is reported to have narrated over 2,000 Hadith.
